title: Energy Management System (EMS) Engineer
description:
The APEX Power Co. Project in Hubbard, TX, currently under Phase 1 construction, is expected to expand to 1\.6 GW. It features a diverse mix of generation technologies, including Siemens SGT\-800/400 simple cycle turbines, MAN/Everllence 18V51/60G gas reciprocating engines, GE LM6000/LM2500 simple cycle turbines, Pratt \& Whitney FT8 simple cycle turbines, and a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), enabling flexible, reliable power output. Future expansion may include additional GE aero and large frame units (6B, 7FA/7FB/7H) in simple or combined cycle configurations, allowing the plant to efficiently meet varying energy demands while supporting data center grid reliability.


**Opportunity Summary**

The Energy Management System (EMS) Engineer provides technical leadership for the plant's Energy Management System (EMS), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), and real\-time operational monitoring systems throughout commissioning and commercial operations. This role supports EMS architecture, system integration, real\-time monitoring of plant generation and electrical system performance, and optimization of power flow, grid connectivity, and dispatch capabilities. Working closely with Operations, Controls Engineering, Electrical Engineering, OEMs, and contractors, the EMS Engineer develops and maintains EMS and SCADA solutions that improve situational awareness, operational reliability, and grid performance.


**As EMS Engineer, your responsibilities specific to the Pre\-Commissioning Phase include:**

* Lead commissioning and functional testing of the Energy Management System (EMS), SCADA, communications infrastructure, and associated monitoring systems to ensure safe and reliable startup.
* Coordinate EMS integration with DCS, PLC, turbine controls, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), electrical systems, and plant instrumentation to support complete operational visibility.

title: Electrical Maintenance Technician
description:
Plains End is a 228 MW natural gas\-fired power generation facility consisting of two reciprocating engine peaking plants. Plains End I began commercial operation in 2002 with 113 MW of generating capacity, followed by the 115 MW Plains End II in 2008\. Together, the facilities provide flexible, reliable generation to help meet regional electricity demand, particularly during periods of peak energy use.


**Opportunity Summary**

The Electrical Maintenance Technician at Plains End plays an important role in ensuring the facility’s natural gas\-fired reciprocating engine generating units remain safe, reliable, and ready for operation. This position performs advanced troubleshooting, testing, maintenance, and technical support for generators, switchyard equipment, control systems, and other plant electrical infrastructure. The Electrical Technician also contributes to outage activities and equipment improvements, shares technical expertise with plant personnel, and helps maintain high standards for safety and regulatory compliance.


**As an Electrical Maintenance Technician, you will support plant operations through the following responsibilities:**


* Provide technical expertise for plant electrical equipment, including generators, excitation systems, transformers, switchgear, switchyard assets, and associated controls.
* Troubleshoot electrical and control system failures, perform root cause analysis, and implement corrective actions to improve equipment reliability.
* Inspect, test, maintain, and troubleshoot electrical and control systems supporting the facility’s reciprocating engine units, including engine starting, fuel gas, synchronization, load control, and protective relaying.
* Perform preventive, predictive, corrective, and emergency maintenance on plant electrical equipment, including high\-voltage and switchyard systems up to 230 kV.
